dublinCore.title: FFT with Two Oscillators
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Superposition
Frequency Analysis
dublinCore.description: Two oscillators, a sine and a cosine, are added and played through the speakers. A triggered 20 ms window shows the sum in the time domain and a live FFT shows its magnitude spectrum from 0 to 2100 Hz, with one peak per oscillator. Sliders set each frequency and amplitude; Start/Pause and Mute control the sound.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Identify the frequency and amplitude of each oscillator from the position and height of its peak in the magnitude spectrum
Explain why the spectrum of a sum of two sinusoids contains one peak for each sinusoid (superposition)
Predict how changing one oscillator's frequency or amplitude changes both the time-domain sum and the spectrum
Demonstrate that the relative phase of the two components changes the shape of the sum but not its magnitude spectrum
Relate the smallest frequency separation at which two peaks can be told apart to the FFT bin width

misconceptions.misconception: Adding a second wave changes the first wave's spectrum
misconceptions.correction: Each sinusoid keeps its own peak; the spectrum of a sum is the sum of the spectra
misconceptions.evidence: With the defaults running, move Cosine Amp from 0 to 1: the 878.9 Hz peak grows while the 439.5 Hz peak stays at 0.49

misconceptions.misconception: Two waveforms that look different must have different spectra
misconceptions.correction: The shape of a sum depends on the relative phase of its components, but the magnitude spectrum does not
misconceptions.evidence: Dragging Cosine Freq to 900 Hz and back to 880 Hz changes the waveform shape while both peak read-outs stay the same

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Two oscillators, a sine and a cosine, are added together. The top plot shows the sum over a 20 millisecond window; the bottom plot shows its magnitude spectrum from 0 to 2100 Hz with one peak for each oscillator. Press Start, then move the four sliders to change each frequency and amplitude.

controls.label: Cosine Amp

visualElements.description: Time-domain plot (green): a 20 ms window of the summed signal, triggered on a rising zero crossing, with a Max |x(t)| read-out
Frequency-domain plot (purple): magnitude spectrum from 0 to 2100 Hz with gold markers on the two strongest peaks
Status indicator (RUNNING / MUTED / PAUSED), peak frequencies and heights, sample rate and bin width

model.description: Two oscillators started at the same instant produce x(t) = A1 sin(2 pi f1 t) + A2 cos(2 pi f2 t). The browser's analyser (via p5.sound) applies a Blackman window and a 16384-point FFT; the sketch plots the magnitude normalised so that an amplitude-1 sine centred on a bin reaches 1 and reports the two strongest local maxima.
equations: x(t) = A1 sin(2 pi f1 t) + A2 cos(2 pi f2 t)
X[k] = (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w[n] x[n] e^{-j 2 pi k n / N}
algorithms: Rising zero-crossing trigger searched over one period of the sum
limitations: The read-out reports the centre of the strongest bin, so it can differ from the slider frequency by up to half a bin (about 1.5 Hz at 48 kHz)
A tone between two bins reads up to about 12% low because of the Blackman window
Two equal tones closer than about 5-6 Hz merge into one peak

instructionalStrategies: Isolating one component by setting the other amplitude to zero
Listening to beats while watching the spectrum
extensions: Add a third oscillator (see the FFT 3 Oscillators MicroSim)
Add a phase slider for the cosine and confirm the magnitude spectrum does not change
